notes:
Account background: large B2B ecommerce platform; building unified conversational assist across merchant dashboards and buyer-facing chat. Interested in Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and strict audit controls. CTO concerned about tail latency during flash sales.

Recent timeline / activities:
- 2025-10-22: Intro call (Maya) — high level requirements captured; asked for baseline latency numbers for 2k concurrent sessions.
- 2025-11-02: Deep dive with infra + security (Omar, Lena) — walked through VPC deployment and KMS options; asked for DR/failover design. Fireflies: ff_20251102_8921.
- 2025-11-15: Pricing pass and initial SOW sent (drive link).
- 2025-11-29: Latency SLO workshop — agreed on per-route SLOs and measurement hooks; Redwood to propose credit mechanics.
- 2025-12-03: POC kickoff call; outlined 4-week Dedicated evaluation plan. Fireflies: ff_20251203_9174.

Use-case & requirements summary:
- Workloads: realtime chat for support agents (bi-directional), high-volume embeddings for semantic search, reranking for product recommendations.
- Throughput targets: steady-state 600 RPS for chat-serving route; peak bursts to 2,500 RPS for short windows (10-20m) during promotions.
- Latency targets: p50 < 40ms (token generation), p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms for chat-short requests; embeddings latency target < 200ms.
- Availability/SLO: Desire 99.95% uptime for Dedicated cluster; per-route latency SLO tiers (gold/silver/bronze) with credits.
- Reserved GPU planning: estimate ~8x A100 equivalent for baseline (mixed precision), ability to burst + autoscale to +50% via reserved buffer or burst pool. Need guidance on mapping token/sec to GPU count across model sizes.
- Reliability/fallbacks: Require documented cross-region failover (active-passive) between us-west-2 and us-east-1 with RTO < 5min for control plane failover and graceful routing to second region. Also want model-variant fallback plan: prefer quantized 8-bit variant when primary full-precision saturates; degrade response length/payload rather than dropping requests.
- Observability: token-level latency traces, per-request model variant tag, per-route cost breakdown, and tracing hooks to correlate with app metrics.
- Security: SSO/SAML, dedicated VPC peering, HSM/KMS for customer keys, audit logs for model inputs/outputs retained per retention policy. EU customer data must stay in EU shard (data residency).

POC milestones and acceptance criteria:
- Week 1: baseline throughput test vs Redwood-provided performance profiles; measure p50/p95/p99 across routes.
- Week 2: failover drill — simulate AZ and region outage; validate reroute and cold-start time for KV cache warming. Acceptance: failover under 5 minutes, <15% error spike.
- Week 3: saturation test — drive to 130% of planned capacity and validate model-variant fallback triggers and SLA crediting. Acceptance: no silent request drops; observable fallback and degraded latencies documented.
- Week 4: security review and SOW finalization; legal to confirm SLA language.

Quotes / call snippets:
- CTO: "Can't risk >5% tail latency spikes during peak checkout flows — must have deterministic fallbacks."
- Head of Infra: "We need mapping of token/sec to GPU for both fp16 and int8 so we can plan reservations and budget."

Open negotiation points / legal asks:
- Precise SLA credit formula for latency SLO breaches (per-route).
- DR runbook inclusion in SOW and annual DR test commitment.
- Clarify support hours for incident escalation and targeted TTR for P1 (30m response, 4h remediation plan).

Next steps (short): Redwood to deliver: 1) detailed GPU sizing worksheet (tokens->GPU) 2) draft DR runbook and failover playbook 3) revised SOW with latency-credit formulas. Legal review slated week of 2025-12-15.
